Eli / Mina — adding the concrete steps here so Opsly engineers can copy/paste. I kept both Python and TS minimal.

TS quickstart (Node 18):
1) unzip redwood-sample-apps-v0.3.zip && cd ts-sample-app
2) cp ../sample-config.env .env && edit .env (set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV=dev, REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwood.ai)
3) npm install
4) npm run dev  # runs local express server with /generate and /embed endpoints

Example fetch (structured output + tool calling):
fetch('/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'Summarize spec and call price_lookup tool', schema: { type: 'object', properties: { summary: { type: 'string' }, price_id: { type: 'string' } } }, tools: [{ name: 'price_lookup', schema: { input: { sku: 'string' }, output: { price: 'number' } } }] })
});

Python quickstart (3.11):
1) unzip && cd py-sample-app
2) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
3) pip install -r requirements.txt
4) cp ../sample-config.env .env && export $(cat .env | xargs)
5) python app.py --mode local

Embedding -> reranker smoke test (both languages):
- Run embed endpoint on the 15 product specs, persist vectors to local SQLite (script included).
- Run the sample reranker endpoint which calls an in-process scoring model (we ship a small BPR-style reranker for dev).

Notes on routing and model choices:
- For the dev lab we'll route to redwood:model-dev-small (low-cost, low-latency) with an automatic fallback to redwood:model-hosted-meduim if sequence lengths exceed 1k tokens.
- Embedding encoder: re-embedding-v1 (fast) for the smoke test. Reranker: rerank-lite-v0 (dev only).

Local cache recommendation:
- Start a redis via docker-compose in sample-apps (we include a compose file). Set REDWOOD_CACHE_URL=redis://localhost:6379 in .env. This emulates the prefix/KV caching layer so your latency numbers are closer to prod.

If you want, I can paste a single-file runnable example during the call. I suggest we add one small CI job to run the smoke tests after the lab so DS can iterate on embeddings.

—Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Integration Runtime
